title: Normal long pass_priority waits at game over surface as critical bridge errors
description:
`pass_priority` logs `game_over after ... idle` as an error when a player is simply waiting through the opponent's turn or timeout, and those lines then get surfaced as top-level export errors.

In `game_20260309_012143_g2`, Gem3P Coach called `pass_priority({"board_cursor":105})` at 02:52:11 while GPT54 Sport still had turns/actions remaining. GPT54 then timed out at 03:00:15. Gem3P's bridge exited normally on game over, but the bridge emitted two ERROR lines and `export_game.py` promoted them into the export's `errors` array even though nothing malfunctioned for Gem3P.

Evidence:
- `~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260309_012143_g2/Gem3P Coach_pilot.log:628` shows the long `pass_priority` wait starting before the opponent timeout.
- `~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260309_012143_g2/game_events.jsonl:566` shows `GPT54 Sport has run out of time, losing the match.`
- `~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260309_012143_g2/Gem3P Coach_mcp.log:125` and `~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260309_012143_g2/Gem3P Coach_mcp.log:130` log `ERROR passPriority game_over after ... idle`.
- `~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260309_012143_g2/Gem3P Coach_errors.log:1` and `~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260309_012143_g2/Gem3P Coach_errors.log:2` show the same lines being copied into the per-player error log that exports consume.

Source:
- `Mage.Client.Bridge/src/main/java/mage/client/bridge/BridgeCallbackHandler.java:3447` treats `lastActionableCallbackAt > 60_000` as abnormal whenever `passPriority` exits on game over.
- That measures time since the last actionable callback, not time since the last callback of any kind, so normal opponent-owned priority windows look "idle".
- `scripts/export_game.py:30` and `scripts/export_game.py:78` do not filter this bridge-specific false positive, so the website surfaces it as a critical error.

Suggested fix:
Do not log this path as an error solely because no actionable callback was seen for 60s. Either key the anomaly detection off `lastCallbackReceivedAt` / a real no-callback stall, or downgrade normal game-over exits to info unless another bridge failure signal is present. Once the bridge logging is corrected, the export should stop surfacing these waits as critical errors.
